Private Pilot Certificate

Start your aviation journey here! The Private Pilot Certificate is your ticket to the skies. Learn how to fly single-engine aircraft safely and confidently. 

Whether you want to fly for fun, travel with your family, or build toward a career, this is the essential first step.

Commercial Pilot Certificate

Take your flying to the professional level. Our Commercial Pilot training will help you refine your flying skills, understand complex maneuvers, and meet the FAA requirements to be paid for flying.

Seaplane Rating

Add water to your flying adventures! Our Seaplane Rating program opens up a whole new world of aviation. Tailwheel Endorsement

Go back to aviation’s roots with a tailwheel endorsement. Tailwheel aircraft demand a higher level of stick-and-rudder skill, making you a more precise and confident pilot. Whether you're looking to improve your landings, explore vintage aircraft, or prepare for bush flying, this endorsement is a smart next step.

Backcountry Flying

Take your skills off the beaten path. Our Backcountry Flying program trains you to land on remote airstrips, navigate rugged terrain, and operate safely in the wilderness.

My philosophy is that the best training comes from a systematic program that has continuity with the aircraft that you fly. As a Large Cabin Test Pilot and former FlightSafety UPRT Instructor, I have the skills to provide that continuity and the best in-aircraft UPRT.

About the Courses

Regulatory Guidance:
According to research conducted by the Royal Aeronautical Society in partnership with ICAO, the CAA, and the FAA, Loss of Control In Flight (LOC-I) is still the leading cause of fatal aircraft accidents, and the only preventative measure is training. The findings from this study were used to produce ICAO Doc 10011 AN/506 First Addition - 2014 Manual on Aeroplane Upset Prevention and Recovery Training.

The training 10g LLC provides is in compliance with and meets the training standards and recommendations found in ICAO Doc 10011.

Methodical Approach:
Our courses use  a methodical approach to upset prevention and recovery training. Psychology, physiology, and advanced aircraft control are primary. A windy river bed that flows in several wide and long, unobstructed directions also means that shifting winds will not likely delay your training. The climate in South Eastern North Carolina affords us the ability to train virtually all year round.

Angel Aviation Sim Center

Now open to the Merrill Field and the Anchorage aviation community to/for:

1.      Maintain Instrument currency and proficiency to facilitate the proper response to inadvertent IMC (instrument meteorological conditions) and avoid a possible CFIT (controlled flight into terrain) accident.
2.      In simulated actual conditions, pilots will refine instrument crosschecks to minimize over controlling the aircraft when actual Instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) are encountered. Teaching the cross checks to transition from IMC to VMC (visual meteorological conditions) at the bottom of an instrument approach when breaking out with runway in sight at decision altitude (DA) or minimum descent altitude (MDA).
3.      Teaching and evaluating instrument emergencies, such as unusual attitudes high and low. Other emergencies include partial panel flight and IAPs. Some emergencies are too dangerous to practice in the aircraft, i.e., engine failures low to the ground.
4.      For pilots flying mostly VMC operations, it is recommended that pilots consider one 2-hour session every 3 months to meet the IAP currency requirements. Leveraging the power of simulation pausing to take advantage of a “teaching moment” improves comprehension and mastery.
5.      And finally, maintaining Instrument currency and proficiency in the Angel Aviation AATD will preclude the higher expense of an aircraft Instrument proficiency Check (IPC).

title: Dubois County Airport Authority
name: Dubois County Airport Authority
description:
The Huntingburg Regional Airport (KHNB),  Huntingburg Airport Technology Park - HATP,  only FBO,  part 61 flight school with N8479F (PA-28-151) are all owned and operated by the Dubois County Airport Authority (DCAA).

The Dubois County Airport Authority, is a local governmental entity established in 1983 per Indiana statue, from the Dubois County Commissioners and the City of Huntingburg. 

The DCAA was forced in taking over the FBO in 2013, when Dubois County Flight Services (subsidiary of a local major corporation) decided to no longer provide the service to the general flying public.

The DCAA attempted to find a private entity to operate the FBO, but due to previous poor decision making (allowing companies to have their own fuel farms) the primary source of revenue was not available to attract private investment. 

Since March of 2013, the DCAA has continued operating the FBO, launched a flight school and continues to expand services to the flying public.

Most recently, the DCAA has partnered with Patoka Valley Career and Technical Cooperative, in creating a high school level program for regional students to start their aviation career!

We are passionate about seeing others in aviation be successful and introduction aviation as a great career choice.

title: Cortez Flying Service, Inc.
name: Cortez Flying Service, Inc.
description:
The story of Cortez Flying Service began in 1948. Before the City of Cortez had an airport, when Vic Reynolds, a World War II bomber pilot, was encouraged by Rollin and Polly Usher to come to Cortez to start a flying service. The original airport location was located two miles south of Cortez, west of the current airport. In 1955, Vic Reynolds, Herb Rose and Milt Bettis formed Cortez Flying Service.

They built the current office building, maintenance building, large hangar and some T-hangars. When the runway was completed they moved into these buildings which Cortez Flying Service still operates out of. After 30 years these buildings reverted to the City.

In 1971, following the death of Herb Rose, Bill Moore and Garth Greenlee purchased Cortez Flying Service. In 1972, current President and co-owner, Robert (Bobby) Yarbrough was hired on as a mechanic after serving in the army in Vietnam. Bobby then obtained his A & P certificate shortly thereafter. • Touch and go activity

• Pennsylvania state government aircraft
• Another state’s government aircraft
• United States’ military aircraft
• “angel” (humanitarian) flights
• Air Ambulance (medical evacuation) flights
• Firefighting aircraft
• Aircraft under 6000 pounds maximum gross landing weight (MLW)
• BTP-based aircraft as stated on a current Aircraft Storage Permit
